After giving this game a 2nd chance after my first initial play though for 5-10 hours, I still can't recommend it. I do recommend Civ 5 and previous Civ games. There's a lot going on, let me give you my take on it...

The tile management in your city is vastly different than previous Civilization games. You are mainly going a wide build, not as 'tall' like prior games. This means your city has hex tiles that are later used for centers like Encampments, Science Buildings, Industrialization buildings, Theatres, Arenas, and so forth. They help your production , culture, science, and other resources. I like the idea of this but it just takes too long. Even if you manage to get your production high in a city, you're still spending anywhere from 4-20 turns on building these types of supplemental buildings. The takeaway is that your city can only focus on one building effort at a time. In the 20 turns it took you to make a Circus or Amusement center, you could have produced more settlers for more towns, or more builders to just work the plots in your land, or even military units to help protect your towns and deal with nearby barbarians. The tradeoff is that if you focus on these centers, you should be able to research faster, produce quicker, and have happier towns.  It works out in the end, but it's just way too time consuming, even on Quick turn speed.

Another issue I have is the barbarians. In my play throughs of almost 30 hours, I cleared tons of camps. Getting some gold helps and keeps your city safe. The problem? They keep coming back! They spawn again (the camps), in random places, even after you clear them! To make it worse, their unit spawning is A LOT more frequent compared to prior Civ games.  Just pumped out 5 horses? Awesome, lets go take that nearby civ! Oh wait, looks like a Barbarian encampment just spawned in between your civ and theirs! And guess what?! IT SPAWNED 3 PIKEMEN! Sorry, calvary, you're already getting outpaced by barbarians! Good luck taking that Civ.  It's moments like these that you feel like the game is out to punish you, even when you try hard to make an effort to do something different. 

The civilizations diplomacy is also a lot more dumbed down. Talking to your nearby AI Civs are just boring. There aren't many options compared to prior Civ games, and usually what they offer is lowballing you for your luxury goods. Most luxury goods (tea, incense, dyes, etc.) should net you around 6-7 gold per minute for 30 turns. In my playthroughs I constantly got low-balled for 1 gold per turn, and when I wanted one of THEIR luxury resources? HA! They want you pay upwards of 30 gold per turn or more! It just doesn't seem fair. 

Then you get denounced for random stuff too, which makes you scratch your head. When an enemy CIV denounces you, can't even denounce them back! It's a pity.  I was denounced for having a 'weak navy' in a game which focuses itself on land expansion with not much water to play around in.  I felt like this game is just slowly finding ways to annoy you and piss you off.

They removed the happiness factor (sorta) and instead towns need amenities to make their citizens content (but its on a city level, not a global scale). This is okay until you realize you have no idea when your town starts NEEDING these amenities. Looks like your 10-20 production town in your early era was doing fine, but here, have a random unhappiness factor and spend 20 turns now to build an Arena for people to enjoy.  It's moments like this that make you scratch your head and think if they could have done something else.

The emphasis on this game feels like it's just a race to build your town with builders improving tiles, and expanding your cities. This is fine until you realize you're spending 100+ turns just to get the FRAMEWORK going. Okay 8 turns to get a science lab, maybe 15 for that arena, now I need an Aqueduct. It's just not efficient. 

The whole time I played this game I kept thinking to myself, "Just one more turn and I'll like this game".  Unfortunately that moment never comes. 

I can't recommend it. I definitely recommend Civ 5, which I think is perhaps the best you're going to get from this series of games by 2K. It's faster, you can build quicker, do more with AI Civs and AI City-States, and enjoy exploring.  

For now, I would stay away from this game. You'll just feel compelled to try and like it when in reality you're just bitter about everything and need to admit it just isn't that good of a game.

# 10,848 Hours Played — And I'd Still Recommend It Without Hesitation

There are games you play, games you finish, and games that become a permanent part of your gaming life. **Civilization VI is the latter for me.**

After more than **10,800 hours**, I think I've earned the right to say this: Civilization VI is one of the most enjoyable and endlessly replayable strategy games I've ever experienced.

What makes this game special isn't simply building cities, commanding armies, researching technologies, or conquering the world. It's how everything works together. Every decision has consequences. Geography matters. Resources matter. Diplomacy matters. Timing matters. The choices you make early in the game can shape the fate of your civilization thousands of years later.

And that's what keeps me coming back.

I love history, strategy, problem-solving, and understanding how complex systems interact. Civilization VI brings all of those interests together beautifully. You aren't just playing against other civilizations; you're constantly balancing competing priorities, adapting to changing circumstances, and trying to build something that will stand the test of time.

**No two games ever feel quite the same.**

Sometimes I want to build a peaceful civilization focused on science, culture, and prosperity. Other times, I want to dominate the map through military strength, economic power, or diplomacy. Sometimes a carefully developed strategy works perfectly. Other times, a neighboring civilization, an unexpected war, or one poor decision sends everything sideways.

That's part of the magic. Even after thousands of hours, there are still different approaches to explore, new challenges to overcome, and opportunities to improve.

I also appreciate something that I think gets overlooked in gaming: Civilization VI rewards patience, curiosity, experimentation, and learning. Failure isn't necessarily the end. It's an opportunity to understand what happened and try something different the next time.

Is it perfect? No game is. But perfection isn't what has kept me playing for over 10,000 hours. It's the depth, freedom, challenge, and sheer enjoyment of building civilizations and watching history unfold differently every time.

And, of course, there's the greatest lie every Civilization player tells themselves:

**"Just one more turn."**

Suddenly, it's three in the morning, you've discovered electricity, your neighbor has declared war, and you're negotiating a trade agreement while planning a railroad across an entire continent.

If you enjoy strategy, history, worldbuilding, or games that make you think, I wholeheartedly recommend Civilization VI.

**10,848 hours later, I'm still having fun.**

And I still have one more turn to play.

**Highly recommended.**

- Todd Jerome Jenkins

Very addictive game with a great modding community. Learning to play the game at a good level and beating deity with most leaders was nearly a full-time job, as a beginner to the series. After beating the game with every leader, I think there's still a lot of learn, optimize and get better at. The unique flavor of the civs is more pronounced here imo and it lets me play with unique gameplay styles, which is why I prefer this over other establishments in this series. The best/worst part of the game is remembering the bonuses with district placement, but can be rewarding in its own way once you remember them with practice. The soundtrack is one to die for, with all the different ages, and civs having different themes which evolve with the era. Late-game yields and clean culture wins, and world building videos are picturesque. The animated characters, and maps are neat for me, though I know most others don't like it as much. 

Civ6 sits as a must-play and a solid entry if you want to get into the 4X genre, and can pay its own worth with hours of gameplay, especially if you're one to explore, try out multiple strategies and game modes, and play with the "Just more turn" mentality
